themes.title: Japan-US joint FX intervention regime — USDJPY 155-158.5 range, intervention credibility test ongoing, BOJ hike Oct/Dec
themes.summary: The G2 coordinated intervention regime remains fully active and is now entering a sustained credibility-test phase on the week of Aug 10. USDJPY opened Monday Aug 10 at 157.89, up 0.08% — technically described as bulls making only a 'timid attempt to recover' from the intervention-induced lows, with far more effort needed to resurrect the uptrend. Recap of the regime: Japan MoF deployed record ¥11.73T in solo intervention across Apr-May 2026 that ultimately failed, with USDJPY hitting a 40-year low near 163-164. On Jul 30 Japan intervened in NY hours. The US Treasury confirmed direct participation on Jul 31 — the first joint US-Japan intervention in nearly 30 years — with Fed NY selling euros for yen via Goldman and Morgan Stanley. USDJPY printed its post-intervention low of 155.20-155.25 on Aug 3. Both Bessent and Trump publicly endorsed further action; Japan MoF confirmed use of the FIMA repo facility, removing the US Treasury-selling tail risk. BOJ voted 8-1 to hold at 1%; with only Takata dissenting for a hike, September appears off the table with October or December more likely for the next BOJ move. UBS flagged that 'Japan's policy mix remains unlikely to generate sustained yen strength' and that the yen 'should continue to be supported more by intervention risk than by domestic monetary fundamentals.' The week of Aug 4-8 confirmed this: USDJPY recovered from the 155.20 low to mid-158s as JPY broadly underperformed on the absence of follow-up intervention — carry traders probing MoF resolve. The Aug 7 NFP (-23K vs +80K, -103K prior revisions) pushed USDJPY back to 157.65, adding a fundamental USD-weakness tailwind to the intervention regime. Bessent reiterated Washington's support for Japan on Aug 7. The Aug 10 session sees USDJPY gravitating back toward 158 — if the pair reclaims 158.5 without official response, carry traders will intensify the test. Japan household spending remains a fundamental drag (-3.3% in June vs +1% expected), complicating BOJ urgency. Structural JPY-positive repatriation flows from Japanese life insurers (foreign holdings ~40% of peak as domestic JGB yields rise) operate independently and are medium-term supportive. Q3 2026 consensus forecasts pin USDJPY at 159, acknowledging the tug-of-war between intervention credibility and fundamental rate differentials.

implications.JPY: MAXIMUM tailwind from dual-authority intervention with FIMA repo mechanism and explicit Bessent re-entry warning, reinforced by catastrophic NFP that structurally weakens the rate-differential argument. But JPY underperformed week of Aug 4-8 when no follow-up intervention materialised — carry traders are probing MoF resolve and the pair has drifted back to 157.89 on Aug 10. BOJ hike Oct/Dec provides a secondary fundamental pillar. All JPY-cross SHORT positions face active G2 headwind but require active monitoring given the absence of follow-up intervention.
implications.USD: ACUTE BEARISH from the Aug 7 NFP shock — broad USD under pressure with EUR/USD above 1.15, GBP/USD near 1.35, DXY near 100. USDJPY at 157.89 and gravitating toward intervention corridor ceiling. USDCHF and USDCAD also suppressed by NFP-driven USD weakness.
implications.EUR: EUR/JPY sold by the mechanism of Fed NY intervention (euros-for-yen). EUR/USD paradoxically firm above 1.15 as USD weakness post-NFP dominates — ING noted this is a USD story, not an EUR story. Q3 consensus targets EUR/USD at 1.16. Watch 1.1560-1.16 as near-term resistance.
implications.GBP: GBP/JPY under dual pressure from intervention and USD-positive-carry unwind. GBP/USD rallied toward 1.3500 on USD weakness; Q3 forecast at 1.35. BoE cutting limits GBP outperformance vs EUR.
implications.CHF: CHF/JPY lower. CHF gains mild safe-haven bid in risk-off environments. USDCHF under pressure from broad USD weakness; Q3 consensus at 0.80.
implications.CAD: CADJPY lower; CAD dynamics primarily driven by Section 338 tariff theme. USD weakness post-NFP partially offsets USDCAD upside and compressed the range further.
implications.AUD: AUDJPY lower. AUD/USD modestly supported by broad USD weakness. Watch AUDJPY 93-94 as intervention-corridor support.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDJPY under pressure from intervention regime.

themes.watchLevel: USDJPY below 155.20 (post-intervention low) = corporate hedger stop-loss loops activate, intervention 'winning' decisively. USDJPY above 158.5 (pre-NFP consolidation high, Aug 10 approaching) = carry trade reasserting, MoF resolve being tested — watch for verbal intervention first. USDJPY back above 160 = market overpowering coordinated defence, theme credibility breaks. Any official MoF/Bessent statement disclaiming further action = theme ends immediately. BOJ hike at Oct or Dec meeting = fundamental support materialises, reduces intervention burden. Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 (Warsh speech) is next major binary for USD direction and hence USDJPY.

themes.title: Warsh Fed under NFP shock — Sep hike odds collapsed, Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 (17 days) is the live USD binary
themes.summary: The Warsh hawkish regime is structurally intact but materially challenged by the Aug 7 NFP disaster, and the market is now in a 17-day positioning window into Jackson Hole with no policy anchor. The Jul 29 FOMC held at 3.5-3.75% with three hawkish dissents; the 30-yr yield surged to 5.21% (19-year high) and Warsh confirmed forward guidance elimination is permanent. Median 2026 dot raised to 3.8%, with 9 of 18 members projecting at least one hike. The Aug 7 NFP print of -23K vs +80K consensus (unemployment 4.1%, prior months revised -103K combined) is the most consequential US labour miss in the current cycle and has directly collapsed Sep hike probability. EUR/USD rose slightly the week of Aug 4-8 and bulls are pressing for more; GBP/USD is consolidating near 1.35; Q3 2026 consensus now targets EUR/USD at 1.16 and GBP/USD at 1.35, reflecting a structurally weaker USD backdrop. The 2026 Jackson Hole symposium runs Aug 27-29 with the official theme 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy.' Warsh stated his keynote speech is 'a blank piece of paper right now' and that he intends to 'step back from near-sighted debates to raise big questions from a broader perspective' — a deliberate signal that he will NOT pre-commit on the near-term rate path. However, post-NFP, markets will force him to address the labour data regardless of his preferred framing. An additional structural uncertainty: Warsh and the Fed are actively contemplating reducing the number of annual FOMC meetings, which would amplify the market impact of each remaining 2026 event. The Fed is 'not constrained by market prices' per Warsh — meaning the NFP disaster does not automatically produce a dovish pivot; he may frame labour weakness as a supply-side or structural phenomenon. Key pre-JH data: US CPI (est. Aug 12-13), PPI, retail sales — any upside CPI surprise partially restores USD. Political dimension: Trump publicly framed the FOMC as obstructionist; a deteriorating labour market intensifies that narrative. Powell, who remains on the Board as a voting member through 2028, adds an additional layer of complexity to the Aug 27-29 communications.

implications.USD: NEAR-TERM BEARISH shock confirmed — EUR/USD above 1.15, GBP near 1.35, DXY near 100. Structural hawkish carry bid now requires Jackson Hole reaffirmation to re-engage. The 17-day void of policy guidance into JH means headline USD pairs will be extremely reactive to any Warsh commentary, CPI/PPI data, and retail sales prints. Q3 consensus targets modest USD stabilisation at current levels.
implications.JPY: Rate differential headwind from Warsh narrative significantly reduced by NFP miss — do not fade JPY strength solely on carry differential. USDJPY bearish case has dual drivers: intervention AND fading hike probability post-NFP.
implications.EUR: EUR/USD headwind from ECB-vs-Fed differential sharply narrowing post-NFP. Bulls pressing above 1.15 but need more effort to extend gains. Q3 target 1.16. Any Warsh dovish pivot at JH = significant EUR/USD upside toward 1.17-1.18.
implications.GBP: GBP/USD consolidating near 1.3500 on broad USD weakness. BoE cutting limits GBP outperformance vs EUR. Q3 target 1.35 — pair is essentially at consensus already, suggesting two-way risk into JH.
implications.CAD: Mixed — USD structural hawkish bid was offsetting CAD tariff weakness; with NFP miss that USD tailwind erodes further. USDCAD range-compressing pre-Aug 19. Aug 19 tariff binary remains the dominant CAD driver.
implications.AUD: Modest headwind from Warsh carry narrative further reduced with NFP. RBA on hold with easing bias; AUD/USD supported by broad USD weakness. Watch AUDUSD for continuation above 0.6600.
implications.NZD: RBNZ same dynamic as AUD. NZDUSD benefits from USD weakness.
implications.CHF: SNB in easing mode; USDCHF under pressure from NFP-driven USD weakness, Q3 consensus at 0.80. CHF may outperform on safe-haven demand in risk-off episodes.

themes.watchLevel: Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 — Warsh keynote (Fri Aug 28) is the primary binary: hawkish signal (hike still on table despite NFP) restores USD carry bid 150-200 pips across board; dovish signal or soft framing extends current USD weakness toward Q3 targets. Pre-JH critical data: US CPI est. Aug 12-13 (any upside surprise partially restores USD), PPI, retail sales. Sep FOMC (Sep 16) is the hard policy event. Any Warsh speech or interview in the 17-day interim that provides hike guidance = major mover. Sub-3.0% CPI print = dovish tolerance returns, theme ends. DXY closing and sustaining below 99.50 = market rejecting hawkish read entirely. 30-yr yield sustained above 5.5% = fiscal concerns overtaking carry narrative.

themes.title: Section 338 Canada tariffs effective Aug 19 — 50% on ~$17.7B of goods, USMCA no shield, 9 days to binary
themes.summary: The Section 338 binary is now 9 days from resolution. Active negotiations are underway — confirmed as of Aug 5-6 — but no deal has been announced and retaliation remains explicitly on the table. Three presidential proclamations signed Jul 20 invoke Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (first modern use since the 1940s) imposing 50% duties on $17.7B of Canadian goods (autos, dairy, alcohol, wine, cement, plywood, furniture, fishing rods, seeds, clothing, hockey sticks, and more) effective August 19, 2026 at 12:01am ET. The duty stacks on top of all existing tariffs and USMCA certification provides zero relief — a structural break from every prior Canada tariff action. Section 338 tariffs carry no statutory time limit, meaning they are permanent unless explicitly revoked. PM Carney said Aug 5 that 'We have time. We have real negotiations, constructive negotiations on multiple issues' but reiterated that 'Canada may retaliate if new tariffs proceed' and 'We have options.' Trump has so far declined to provide any Section 232 relief to Canada in strategic sectors, and Carney is seeking a deal that removes Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminium, autos, and lumber — a significantly broader ask than simply pausing Section 338. Alberta Premier Smith has explicitly opposed using energy as a retaliatory weapon (protecting Line 5), which limits Carney's retaliatory toolkit. USDCAD price action: resistance at 1.4080 stopped bulls in their tracks for a second consecutive weekly decline, with the pair settling near 1.3942 on Aug 7 after the NFP-driven USD collapse. The NFP shock has created a countervailing USD-weakness drag that has compressed the USDCAD range below 1.40, making the pre-Aug 19 positioning even more binary-dependent. Per Global Trade Alert, Canada's average US tariff rises 1.89 percentage points overnight to 6.27% if Section 338 lands as scheduled. Section 338's precedent matters beyond the tariffs themselves: a dormant statute now overrides a trade agreement's core preference on a presidential finding alone, setting a template for future use.

implications.CAD: STRONG structural headwind — 50% stacking duties on $17.7B of exports, permanent statutory authority, no USMCA exemption, and active retaliation threat from Carney. USDCAD technically capped at 1.4080 resistance (two weekly drops in a row) with NFP-driven USD weakness adding to the downside compression — pair trading near 1.3942. Aug 19 binary outcome: deal struck = sharp CAD relief 100-150 pips; tariffs land = USDCAD gaps higher 100-150 pips; Canadian retaliation = vol surge 100+ pips both directions. Widen stops, reduce size on all CAD crosses.
implications.USD: Moderate tariff-narrative tailwind from USDCAD, but Aug 7 NFP shock creates significant countervailing USD weakness. Net: USDCAD consolidating 1.39-1.41 range ahead of Aug 19 binary rather than trending.
implications.MXN: Elevated secondary exposure — USDMXN moves can telegraph CAD next-session. Mexico separately facing Section 301 successor regime at 10-12.5%.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EU separately under 15% tariff ceiling from Jul 1; EU-Canada trade linkage adds modest contagion risk to EUR crosses in a CAD-shock scenario.
implications.AUD: Indirect risk-off if CAD volatility spills into broader commodity bloc on Aug 19; AUDCAD may be volatile around the binary.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD may see vol spike around Aug 19.

themes.watchLevel: Aug 19 12:01am ET is the primary hard binary — 9 days away. Active negotiations confirmed (Carney Aug 5: 'constructive negotiations on multiple issues') — deal struck pre-Aug 19 = sharp CAD relief 100-150 pips, retire theme. Tariffs land as scheduled = USDCAD gaps higher 100-150 pips, extend CAD-bearish bias. Canada retaliation proclamation published = CAD vol surge 100+ pips both directions. Any Section 338 legal challenge or court injunction = uncertainty spike. 1.4080 is the key technical ceiling for USDCAD — bulls need to reclaim it to signal tariff-risk pricing returning. USDCAD support at 1.3900 (watch carefully given NFP-driven USD softness). Section 338's permanent nature means theme does not auto-expire on Aug 19 even if tariffs land — persists until explicitly revoked or deal supersedes.
